vulkanmod.options.windowMode.tooltip: Controls how Minecraft uses the display. Exclusive fullscreen can reduce desktop-compositor overhead, while windowed fullscreen makes switching apps faster.
vulkanmod.options.resolution.tooltip: Sets the output resolution used in exclusive fullscreen. Higher resolutions look sharper but require more GPU work and video memory.
vulkanmod.options.refreshRate.tooltip: Sets the monitor refresh rate used in exclusive fullscreen. Higher rates can display more frames when the monitor and GPU can keep up.
vulkanmod.options.framerateLimit.tooltip: Caps how many frames Minecraft renders each second. A sensible cap reduces GPU load, heat, and power use and can make frame pacing steadier; Max removes the cap.
vulkanmod.options.vsync.tooltip: Synchronizes displayed frames with the monitor to prevent screen tearing. It may add input latency and limits FPS to the active refresh rate.
vulkanmod.options.guiScale.tooltip: Changes the size of menus, text, and the HUD without changing the 3D render resolution. Auto selects a scale for the current window size.
vulkanmod.options.gamma.tooltip: Adjusts scene brightness so dark areas are easier or harder to see. This has no meaningful performance cost.
vulkanmod.options.viewBobbing.tooltip: Moves the camera slightly while walking and sprinting. Disable it for a steadier view; performance is effectively unchanged.
vulkanmod.options.attackIndicator.toolti: Chooses where the melee attack-cooldown indicator appears, or hides it. This changes only the HUD.
vulkanmod.options.autosaveIndicator.tool: Shows an icon while the world is being saved. Disabling the icon does not disable autosaving or remove save-related pauses.
vulkanmod.options.performancePreset.tool: Applies a coordinated group of graphics and VulkanMod settings. Potato favors speed, Balanced mixes quality and performance, Quality favors visuals, and changing an individual preset setting switches to Custom.
vulkanmod.options.advCulling.tooltip: Skips chunk sections hidden behind terrain. Aggressive removes the most work but may cause visible pop-in; Conservative is safer, and Off renders every section inside the camera view.
vulkanmod.options.ao.tooltip: Controls block-corner shading. Off uses flat lighting, On uses smooth lighting, and ON (Sub-block) improves shading on partial blocks with extra rebuild cost and experimental visuals.
vulkanmod.options.deviceSelector.tooltip: Selects the GPU VulkanMod uses. Auto is recommended; changing the device takes effect after restarting Minecraft. Current device: %s
vulkanmod.options.entityCulling.tooltip: Stops drawing entities in chunk sections that are not visible. This can greatly help in crowded areas and changes rendering only, not entity simulation.
vulkanmod.options.frameQueue.tooltip: Sets how many frames Vulkan may keep in flight. Higher values can keep the GPU busier and smooth some stalls, but use more memory and add input latency; 2 is the most responsive.
vulkanmod.options.indirectDraw.tooltip: Submits many terrain draws through fewer CPU calls. It usually helps when the CPU or driver is the bottleneck, but can add GPU or driver overhead and requires supported hardware.
vulkanmod.options.adaptiveChunkUploads.t: Smoothly adjusts chunk preparation and upload budgets using measured chunk cost and Vulkan backpressure after recent transfers. It ignores unrelated FPS drops, recovers gradually, and never exceeds the configured ceiling.
vulkanmod.options.chunkUploadsPerFrame.t: Sets the hard maximum number of completed chunk sections uploaded in one frame. Higher values reveal terrain faster but can create transfer or GPU-fence spikes; Adaptive mode may temporarily use fewer.
vulkanmod.options.renderDistance.tooltip: Controls how many chunks are drawn around the camera. Higher distances show more terrain but increase chunk building, CPU use, GPU load, and memory use.
vulkanmod.options.simulationDistance.too: Controls how far chunks keep ticking entities, redstone, and crops. In single-player this directly increases integrated-server CPU work; multiplayer is also limited by the server.
vulkanmod.options.prioritizeChunkUpdates: Controls how urgently visible chunk meshes are completed. Threaded gives smoother movement but may show terrain later; blocking modes reveal updates sooner and can cause larger frame stalls.
vulkanmod.options.graphics.tooltip: Controls Minecraft's main visual-quality effects. Fancy improves foliage and other effects; Fast reduces rendering work for higher FPS.
vulkanmod.options.particles.tooltip: Controls how many effect particles are created and drawn. Lower settings reduce CPU and GPU work during combat, weather, explosions, and busy farms.
vulkanmod.options.renderClouds.tooltip: Controls cloud rendering quality. Fancy clouds have more depth and cost more GPU time; Fast is cheaper, and Off removes cloud rendering.
vulkanmod.options.biomeBlendRadius.toolt: Blends grass, foliage, and water colors across nearby biomes. Larger areas make borders smoother but increase chunk rebuild time.
vulkanmod.options.entityShadows.tooltip: Draws simple shadows beneath entities. Disabling them provides a small GPU saving in areas with many mobs or players.
Scales how far entities remain visible. Higher percentages show distant entities but increase CPU and GPU work, especially in crowded scenes.
vulkanmod.options.mipmapLevels.tooltip: Creates lower-resolution texture copies for distant blocks. Higher levels reduce shimmering but use more video memory and require a texture reload when changed.
vulkanmod.options.uniqueOpaqueLayer.tool: Uses a dedicated combined layer for solid terrain to reduce render-state and draw overhead. Changing it rebuilds chunks and unusual shader or rendering mods may prefer it disabled.
vulkanmod.options.particleCulling.toolti: Skips redundant particles using distance, camera direction, and same-type limits. Quality is conservative, Balanced removes more, Performance is most aggressive, and Off draws every generated particle.
vulkanmod.options.blockEntityCulling.too: Stops drawing chests, signs, spawners, and other block entities when they are outside the camera view or too distant. Their game logic continues running normally.
vulkanmod.options.leavesCulling.tooltip: Removes hidden faces between adjacent leaf blocks, reducing forest geometry substantially. Transparent resource packs may make the visual difference more noticeable.
vulkanmod.options.textureAnimations.tool: Updates animated textures such as water, lava, fire, and portals. Disabling it makes those textures static and reduces animation-update work.
vulkanmod.options.renderScale.tooltip: Renders the 3D scene at a percentage of the window resolution, then scales it to the display. Lower values greatly reduce GPU load but make the world look softer; the interface stays readable.
vulkanmod.options.builderThreads.tooltip: Controls background chunk-building workers. Auto leaves CPU headroom for Minecraft and the integrated server; higher manual values can build chunks faster but compete with other work.
vulkanmod.options.backfaceCulling.toolti: Skips hidden block faces and culls the back side of opaque terrain. Disable only for models with incorrectly missing faces; disabling increases terrain geometry.
vulkanmod.options.wayland.tooltip: Forces GLFW's native Wayland backend on Linux when supported. Restart Minecraft after changing this option.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
vulkanmod.diagnostics.empty: Open Diagnostics to capture the current status.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.benchmark.tooltip: Closes settings, counts down for three seconds, then measures ten seconds of normal gameplay.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.benchmark.unavaila: Join a world before running the performance snapshot.
Apply or undo pending settings first.
A performance snapshot is already running.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.benchmark.failed: Performance snapshot failed because too few frames were captured.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.benchmark.stale.va: World context or settings changed since this run
vulkanmod.diagnostics.session.truncated: %s more entries omitted from this capture
vulkanmod.diagnostics.issue.mod_inventor: Loaded mod details could not be read
vulkanmod.diagnostics.flag.requested_una: Requested, but unavailable in this build
Confidence: %s | performance impact: %s | visual impact: %s | restart: %s
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.incomp: No VulkanMod setting can resolve another renderer replacement. Update or remove that renderer, or use it in a separate profile.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.mod_in: Refresh once. If the inventory still fails, copy the report and include it when reporting the problem.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.runtim: Investigate the suppressed mod or graphics failure
VulkanMod isolated a compatibility-call failure. Update the relevant mod and copy this report; settings cannot repair an exception or a failed graphics call.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.missin: Update the mod requesting unsupported graphics functions
A requested graphics function is missing or limited. Copy the report and update the mod; the troubleshooting baseline can only reduce other variables.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.gl_con: VulkanMod used a fallback for an incomplete graphics contract. Copy the report if the same scene has visual problems.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.versio: Update or roll back the listed mod to the verified version family. This warning does not change its runtime compatibility mode.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.unknow: The mod is recognized, but its version could not be verified. Check the installed file before troubleshooting rendering behavior.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.conser: Troubleshooting only: switch up to three rendering conditions to conservative values, retest the same scene, then use Undo before Apply if the preview is not acceptable. Restoring native render scale can substantially increase GPU work. This does not fix missing APIs.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.rule.benchm: The current snapshot shows uneven frame pacing. Compare deliberate changes in the same scene; a short snapshot cannot prove a universal improvement.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.preview.sco: Stages settings only; mods, compatibility modes, and render-path ownership are unchanged
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.succe: %s change(s) staged. Use Apply to commit or Undo to discard.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.appli: Doctor changes applied. Run another snapshot in the same scene for comparison.
Doctor changes applied. No fresh before snapshot was available, so no comparison will be shown.
Doctor changes applied, but the world, window, or settings context changed before Apply. The saved baseline was discarded.
Settings changed after the Doctor preview. The changes were applied, but no comparison baseline was saved.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.draft: The staged settings no longer match the Doctor preview, so its comparison plan was discarded. Your remaining drafts are preserved.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.block: Apply or undo the existing staged settings before using this action.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.stage.resul: Settings changed after the preview. Refresh Diagnostics and review the new plan.
Apply or undo the existing staged settings first.
A required setting is unavailable in this screen.
The proposed action was rejected by the safe-setting allowlist.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.n: Run a current-settings snapshot before staging Doctor changes to save a baseline.
No fresh baseline was available when these changes were staged.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.b: Fresh baseline saved; use Apply before running the after snapshot.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.a: Baseline saved. Run another snapshot after applying the staged changes.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.r: Comparable before and after snapshots are available.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.c: The world, dimension, or window context changed; these snapshots are not compared.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.s: Settings no longer match the confirmed Doctor plan; run a new baseline.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.i: A snapshot contains invalid or insufficient measurements.
vulkanmod.diagnostics.doctor.benchmark.d: Short snapshots are directional; repeat them in the same scene. Differences under 2% and isolated long frames are treated as normal noise. The Doctor does not claim that a setting fixed compatibility.
